title: AI infrastructure, power and the digital economy

paras: Technology, infrastructure, network architecture, institutional ownership and business economics.
5G, fiber and edge platforms, GPUs/TPUs, high-bandwidth memory, AI clusters, foundation models, inference APIs, agent workflows, zero-trust controls and observability.

blocks.h2: Who developed, funded, owned and operated the systems?
paras: Semiconductor designers and foundries, hyperscalers, AI developers, carriers, energy suppliers, regulators, enterprises and public agencies. These participants had different roles: research sponsorship, equipment supply, network operation, regulation, standardization and service consumption should not be conflated.
Distributed accelerator fabrics and data centers interconnected with cloud, mobile and enterprise networks; latency, energy, security and governance are design constraints.
Accelerator capacity, inference tokens or usage, software subscriptions, integration services, enterprise automation and managed security.
AI services are applications on digital infrastructure; AI-assisted network operations are different from networks carrying AI traffic or AI-agent messages.

An AI assistant request may traverse mobile access, CDN or API gateway, identity controls, model routing and an accelerator cluster. Monitoring, power delivery and data governance are as critical as model weights.
AI infrastructure involves foundry capacity, accelerators, electricity, cooling, interconnection, software distribution, privacy rules and industry-specific compliance.
